chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Husayn from Hammad ibn Isa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A man pays the Zakat al-Fitr on behalf of his Mukatab (freed slave paying installments), his wife's slave, his Christian slave, his Magian (Zoroastrian) slave, and whoever is enclosed under his roof.

key_terms.زَكَاةَ الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (alms of breaking the fast)
key_terms.مَا أَغْلَقَ عَلَيْهِ بَابَهُ: Whoever is enclosed under his roof/household
key_terms.مُكَاتَبِهِ: His Mukatab (a slave who has contracted for his freedom by paying a sum)

ai.seo_question: Who can a man pay Zakat al-Fitr for according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the obligation of Zakat al-Fitr extends beyond free Muslims to include the *Mukatab* (slave negotiating freedom), the wife’s slave, and non-Muslim slaves (Christians or Magians) under the head of household's authority. This reflects the Shia juristic view that the provider bears the responsibility for those in his direct care, regardless of their specific religious status, ensuring the purifying charity reaches all dependents within the domestic sphere.
